headline: Katmai camera and historical observation patterns

insights.title: Highest camera detection rate
insights.detail: 19.13 of every 100 sampled frames had an accepted detection (95% interval 14.09-25.44).
insights.caveat: This short collection does not estimate animal abundance.

insights.title: Peak public observation month
insights.detail: 239 GBIF records, or 32.7% of records with a month.
insights.caveat: GBIF counts reflect visitor access, observer effort, and reporting as well as bear presence.

insights.title: Conditions on historical observation days
insights.detail: Observation days averaged 16.0 daylight hours, 3.9 mm precipitation, and 85.6% relative humidity.
insights.caveat: These are associations in opportunistic records, not causes or forecast probabilities.

limitations: Detection rates describe sampled frames, not animal abundance or population size.
Consecutive frames are correlated and may show the same animal repeatedly.
The sighting cooldown can merge repeated detections and lower observed rates.
Capture time is not observation time when a live page is replaying highlights.
One short collection window cannot support seasonal or hour-of-day forecasts.
NPS inventory presence does not mean a species is visible from these cameras.
GBIF record counts reflect observer effort and publication bias, not animal abundance.
The GBIF regional envelope is not the legal boundary of Katmai National Park and Preserve.
NASA POWER weather is gridded data at one Katmai coordinate, not a camera-site weather station.
Calculated daylight is an astronomical approximation and does not include terrain or cloud cover.
A day without a GBIF record is not a confirmed day without bears.
